column2: “Already?{p}
Let's stay alone together a little longer.”
And then, all sorts of things and more things…!
you're not thinking anything weird, are you?”
“N-no, I'm not thinking anything!”
I shook my head frantically.
“…You're suspicious.
You might be more dangerous than the people outside.{r}{p}I'm going downstairs after all.”
{n2} said it flatly, stood up, and left the room before I could stop her.
I had no choice but to follow her.
In the common room downstairs, a few people were relaxing until dinner started.
Could it be the ghost of a man who died in the snow?
“Nothing, really…”
I played dumb.
But the man hadn't missed the glance that {n2} and I exchanged.
“Something did happen, didn't it?”
“N-no,
it was nothing much…”
I denied it in a hurry.
What on earth does this guy want to know?
Mr. Kobayashi's words only fed my curiosity.
“Twenty years ago…
What exactly happened back then?”
I asked, looking back and forth between Mr. Kobayashi and Mr. Mikimoto.
“It's none of your business.
…{n2}, we're leaving.”
“Wait, Uncle!{p}
I want to hear it too.”
I felt I couldn't leave her alone now.
you don't have to take what that guy says seriously.{r}{p}He's just making it up as he goes.”
I spoke desperately through the door.
I strained my ears, but no reply came.
“Hey {n2}, are you listening?{r}{p}You didn't actually believe that stuff, did you?”
“Please, just leave me alone!”
{n2} cried in a hysterical tone.
Hearing her voice, I thought it'd be best to leave her alone until she calmed down a little.
I looked away and started explaining.
“…I'm not…
really sure, but {g}
something terrible happened…”
“Something terrible?”
“…That Tanaka guy…
well…
it seems he's been killed.”
I cautiously approached the door and listened to the sounds inside.
“S-somebody!
Somebody come here!”
Mr. Kayama's voice reached me.
What on earth was going on in there?
I felt I didn't want to open the door, but I couldn't afford to hesitate.
Making up my mind, I reached for the knob.
“Somebody, please take care of these people.”
When Mr. Mikimoto pointed to the fallen Kayamas, Midori and Toshio, who had been outside, finally came in timidly.
Haruko was also bleeding heavily, and she didn't look like she'd survive.
Treating her seemed pointless.
But my only worry was {n2}.
Led by Mr. Mikimoto, I took {n2} to her room.
no, it's not like that.”
I thought we still couldn't be called a couple, so I answered that way.
“But you like her, don't you?”
Mr. Mikimoto pressed further.
“…Yes.”
I answered honestly.
“Not really…
she's not my type.”
Embarrassed, I lied.
“Hmm…
I see.{r}{p}Guess I got the wrong idea.{r}{p}Then it can't be helped.
I can't drag outsiders into this.{r}{p}Looks like I'll have to look after her myself.”
Outsiders?
What did he mean?
He was an outsider himself…
“Now, leave the room.{r}{p}I'll do everything I can.”
“What exactly are you…?”
He grinned and took out something like a pendant.

It seemed to have been just a cross on a chain originally, but now it jangled with a charm from some shrine,{p}a wooden carving with a face like a moai, supposedly against evil,{p}animal fangs, blue stones, and other odds and ends.
“What on earth is that…?”
When I asked, he answered with a perfectly straight face.
“Well.
I prepared it in case something like this happened.{r}{p}Evil spirits, you know, who can tell what works on them?{r}{p}With all this, one of them is bound to protect us.”
…He might be rather sloppy.
“…Now, you should leave, it's dangerous.”
I couldn't bring myself to leave.
“What's wrong?{r}{p}
There's no reason to risk your neck for someone who's neither your girlfriend nor your type.{r}{p}Come on, leave me alone.”
“…I'll protect her.”
“What did you say?”
“I said I'll protect her.{r}{p}I will definitely protect {n2}.”
I thought he'd laugh at me.
Mr. Mikimoto looked at my face in silence for a while, then smiled, seemingly relieved.
“My eyes didn't deceive me.{r}{p}I knew you'd say that.{r}{p}Now, take this…”
He held out that jumbled lucky-charm pendant.
I reluctantly took it.
“Sorry, but I have other things to do.{r}{p}Could you keep an eye on her for a while?”
“…Yes.”
After Mr. Mikimoto left, I looked at the pendant more closely and saw it even had a charm reading “Safe Childbirth.”
I wondered if it was a good idea to rely on a person like that, but now there was no other choice.
I told myself he at least had initiative and a cool head, and hung the chain around my neck.
With the pendant around my neck, I approached the bed and looked down at {n2}, who looked dead.
I left the room obediently.
The moment the door shut behind me, I desperately wanted to be at {n2}'s side after all.
…But going back now to say “I actually like {n2}”
felt wrong somehow.
Mr. Mikimoto seemed to have a plan,
so I should just leave it to him.
I decided to go back to Mr. Kayama's room and look inside.
Toshio and Midori had laid the Kayamas on the bed and were treating their wounds, covered in blood.
It looked like a field hospital.
Neither of them even looked up when I came in.
will they be okay?”
I asked, but Toshio shook his head with a grim face.
“…If only there were a doctor.”
Since there wasn't one, that meant there was no saving them…
I looked around for Mr. Kobayashi; he wasn't helping, just crouching in a corner of the room holding his head.
“Mr. Kobayashi…
what on earth is happening?”
I put the question to him with a bit of irritation.
His hollow eyes looked up at me.
“A moment ago you called out to {n2} as Miyuki, didn't you?{r}{p}Was what Mr. Mikimoto said true?{r}{p}That {n2}'s…
{n2}'s real mother died?”
“…I don't know
…I don't know anything…”
Mr. Kobayashi shook his head violently, then held his head again and began to tremble.
I was about to press Mr. Kobayashi further when it happened.
Someone screamed, and the next moment the whole building was shaking violently.
an earthquake?!”
The violent shaking sent me sprawling on the floor.
It was a strange kind of shaking, as if the building itself were screaming and writhing.
The floor creaked, the walls cracked, and splinters of wood fell from the ceiling.
This was no ordinary earthquake.
Could {n2}…
have something to do with this?
I tumbled out of the door into the hallway.
Staggering left and right as if on a bus, I ran down the violently shaking hallway toward {n2}'s room.
The moment I got there, the door burst open and Mr. Mikimoto rushed out.
It's terrible!”
“Did something
happen to {n2}?”
I noticed a streak of blood running down Mr. Mikimoto's forehead.
“…I tried to stop her…
but it was no use.{r}{p}No one can stop her anymore…
She'll kill everyone!”
He was panicking, and I couldn't follow what he was saying.
“Calm down, Mr. Mikimoto.{r}{p}What happened?”
The shaking stopped suddenly.
Peering cautiously into {n2}'s room through the open door, I saw the window broken and the curtains flapping in the snow blowing in.
Noticing my gaze, Mr. Mikimoto nodded and spoke.
“Miyuki hadn't left {n2} yet.{r}{p}She lulled us into lowering our guard and then attacked, but in the end she went out through the window.{r}{p}Without this charm, I'd have been killed.”
He showed me the charm pendant around his neck.
“Outside…?”
“Yes.
But I think she'll be back soon.{r}{p}If she finds anyone defenseless, she'll attack again.{r}{p}We'd better gather everyone somewhere.”
What a mess…!
Would {n2} remain possessed by that evil spirit forever?
Was there… anything I could do?
I decided to go outside and look for {n2}.
I rushed into the room, stuck my head out the window, and looked around.
I shouted, but all that came back was the howl of the raging blizzard.
I ran out of the room.
Mr. Mikimoto called after me.
What are you going to do?”
“…I'm going to look for her.{r}{p}For {n2}…
I have to save {n2}…”
“Even though you don't like her?”
“…Earlier,
I just lied.”
I could feel my face turning red.
Mr. Mikimoto, seemingly noticing nothing, said to me.
“What can you possibly do by rushing blindly outside?{r}{p}…She will definitely come back sooner or later.{r}{p}Wait for that moment.”
Now that he said it, I had no way to argue.
Suppressing my restlessness, I decided to gather everyone in the common room again with Mr. Mikimoto.
I ran off to gather everyone as quickly as possible.
“Everyone!
Please gather here!{p}
It's dangerous!
Hurry and gather!”
Thinking they might have gone back to their rooms, I shouted while pounding on doors.
As people timidly came together, Mr. Mikimoto told them to gather in the common room.
They were probably anxious already, and everyone obediently followed his confident tone.
As for the Kayamas, we judged it dangerous to move them and left them as they were.
No one said it aloud, but everyone must have thought that even if they were attacked again, with no doctor there was no hope for them anyway.
Nine of us were assembled in the common room: the Kobayashis, Toshio, Midori, the three office ladies, Mr. Mikimoto and me.
We sat huddled together, and one of the three girls, Keiko, was the first to speak anxiously.
“What…
what on earth is going on here?”
Mr. Mikimoto and I looked at each other.
Would they believe us if we talked about {n2}'s birth secret and evil spirits?
Mr. Mikimoto seemed to have the same thought.
“I can't say for certain what's happening.{r}{p}All I know is that one person was torn apart and killed by something, and two more are gravely injured.{r}{p}And that something
must still be near this building, waiting for a chance to attack us.”
I heard several people gulp.
The girls covered their mouths, looking close to tears.
Toshio glared at Mr. Kobayashi and said.
“Boss, you know something, don't you?{r}{p}That thing…
wasn't that {n2}'s doing?”
I couldn't help cutting in.
“That's {n2}'s mother's evil spirit!
{n2} has done nothing wrong!”
“An evil spirit?”
Toshio asked back, looking like he thought I'd lost my mind.
“An evil spirit, he says!
Ha!
There's no such thing!”
The moment he said that, Toshio seemed to rise to his feet.
And with the very momentum of his rising, Toshio's body flew up into the air.
Startled, we looked up and saw {n2} clinging to the ceiling, hoisting Toshio up with her long hair like a rope.
Toshio kicked his legs wildly, trying to shake off the hair wrapped around his neck.
Screams and sobs filled the air.
stop, {n2}!”
My voice was drowned out by a terrible, heart-wrenching cry full of sorrow and rage.
'I'll kill you…!'
“Eeeee-
eeek!”
Mr. Kobayashi let out a pitiful scream and ran toward the entrance.
The hair around Toshio's neck suddenly loosened, and his body was slammed onto the floor.
Mr. Kobayashi, in just his socks, dropped down onto the dirt floor and threw himself at the inner sliding door.
He seemed to be trying to escape outside.
'I won't forgive you…'{g}
{n2}'s eyes turned sharply toward Mr. Kobayashi.
Mr. Kobayashi tried desperately to flee, but for some reason his legs wouldn't move.
Black hair like a snake was stretching toward his neck as he turned around with a look of terror.
I heard several people scurrying off to the dining room in the confusion, but I couldn't even turn around.
'Murderer…'
The black hair whipped like a lash and struck Mr. Kobayashi's body.
“Aaah!”
His clothes tore diagonally from shoulder to waist, exposing skin.
Blood spattered everywhere.
stop, please!”
Next, a flash aimed at his face.
His shielding arms were slashed open and Mr. Kobayashi screamed.
Crack, crack, it tore at his body as if tormenting him, and with each strike blood flew.
Onto my feet, and my cheek too…
Frozen with fear, I could only watch the scene, unable to do anything.
'Why did you kill her…?'
“Th-
that was a mistake!{p}I only took the payoff money because my father asked me to!{p}If she hadn't made a scene, it never would have come to that!{p}It wasn't my fault!”
Mr. Kobayashi began to scream this, spraying foam from his mouth.
'The payoff money'…?
'It wasn't my fault'?
Could it be…!
“You killed her.”
Mr. Mikimoto said in a surprisingly calm voice.
Mr. Kobayashi held his head in his blood-covered hands, rubbing it against the dirt floor as if bowing in apology, trembling and repeating the same words again and again.
“It wasn't my fault…”
More than {n2} looking like a demon woman, more than the unscientific phenomena beyond all common sense, what shocked me most was that Mr. Kobayashi was the one who had killed {n2}'s mother.
The blizzard outside had grown quiet at some point, and the room was filled with a terrifying silence.
I stared at Mr. Kobayashi, forgetting even to breathe.
Breaking that silence, that voice rang out again.
'I won't forgive you…'{g}
Mr. Kobayashi started, lifted his face, hideously twisted with terror, and looked at {n2} floating in the air.
'I will never forgive you!'
At that moment, {n2}'s whole body seemed to blaze up in pale blue flames.
{n2}'s hair, wreathed in pale blue flames, slithered out toward the neck of Mr. Kobayashi, who had collapsed at the entrance.
Mr. Kobayashi stared at the hair as if bewitched, unable to stir.
In that instant, Mr. Mikimoto threw the charm from around his neck at {n2} in the air.
The moment it hit {n2},
the charm flashed as brilliantly as a camera flash.
An agonized cry, as if from the depths of the earth, burst from {n2}'s mouth.
That sloppy charm had really worked.
But when the charm fell to the floor, {n2} turned her rage from Mr. Kobayashi to Mr. Mikimoto.
The black hair stretched out like a giant serpent and coiled around Mr. Mikimoto's neck.
Having lost the charm that had protected him, Mr. Mikimoto was left helpless, hoisted as if crucified.
'I won't let you get in my way…'
“Ugh…
S-sis…”
Sis…?
no, the evil spirit seemed to falter as well.
{n2}'s mother was Mr. Mikimoto's sister?
“It's me,
Yosuke.{r}{p}Sis,
you're Miyuki, aren't you?”
'Yosuke…'
Her earlier rage had turned to bewilderment.
I looked back and forth between Mr. Mikimoto and the charm on the floor.
The charm kept glowing faintly on the floor.
Mr. Mikimoto kept talking.

“I happened to be at my aunt's house and escaped the disaster, and since I was still little then, no one told me what had happened to my sister, my father, and my mother.{r}{p}I learned the details after I graduated from high school.
I also learned that everyone in the village knew who the culprit was and pretended not to.{r}{p}And the police were the same.{r}{p}I made up my mind.
To take revenge with my own hands.”
The black hair binding Mr. Mikimoto shrank back with a hiss and withdrew.
'Avenge us…
Avenge us on our enemy…'
Mr. Mikimoto shook his head.
“I don't intend to kill him.{r}{p}I only wanted to bring the truth to light.{r}{p}Legally, the statute of limitations has run out anyway.”
'That…
I won't allow that!'
It was as if the room, no, the whole building, cried out in rage.
The floor creaked, the walls bowed, and the ceiling shook.
'I'll kill you all!'
“Stop it, Sis!{p}
…Whoa!”
Cracks ran across the ceiling and splinters of wood rained down.
The windowpanes shattered and the blizzard blew in.
{n2}'s hair multiplied before our eyes, stretching tentacles in every direction.
Kyoko, Toshio, and Midori were all caught in it.
I ran for the charm on the floor.
But {n2}'s hair coiled around my neck.
I hurriedly jammed my fingers in, but it tightened, crushing my throat until I couldn't even groan.
“Stop, Sis!{p}
If you wish for {n2}'s happiness, stop now!”
For an instant the squeezing loosened.
Prying it open with my fingers, I pulled my head out and rolled across the floor to lunge for the charm.
Almost the instant I picked it up, pale blue flames shot from {n2}'s body toward me.
Shutting my eyes, I held the charm up before my face.
I braced for intense heat and impact, but felt nothing.
Timidly opening my eyes, I saw the charm catching the pale blue flames.
Or rather, the flames shrank rapidly just before reaching the charm and vanished.
Summoning my courage, I stood up and approached {n2}, holding the charm high.
As if the charm were draining their energy, the pale blue flames faded and {n2}'s body gradually descended.
My daughter…'
“She's not only your daughter!{p}
She's the daughter of my brother-in-law Ichiro and you!”
Mr. Mikimoto cried out in anguish through his tears.
{n2}'s body jerked in midair.
'…Ichiro…'
Staggering, I moved closer to her.
Her bloodied chest was at eye level.
Her face was turned up toward the ceiling, her eyes rolled white.
The evil spirit…
no, Miyuki's spirit had clearly lost its malice by now.
But I didn't know what I should do, and I stood there flustered, still clutching the charm.
I called out the name most precious to me.
Calling her name seemed to snap the restraint in my mind.
Without thinking at all, I hugged her body floating in the air with all my strength.
The moment our bodies touched, a dazzling light and an explosive shock nearly blew me away.
I wrapped both arms firmly around her back and clung on desperately.
The charm in my hand grew too hot to hold, but I gritted my teeth and endured.
'Noooooo!'{g}
A scream that sounded like neither {n2} nor her mother echoed through the room.
“Give {n2}…
give {n2} back!”
I shouted at the top of my lungs.
The next instant, {n2}'s whole weight, no longer floating, bore down on me and I staggered backward and fell.
{n2}'s body was limp and motionless as if dead, and terribly heavy.
The last pale blue flames that had faintly enveloped {n2} left her and drifted vaguely in the air.
For an instant that flame seemed to take human form, but when I blinked and strained my eyes, there was nothing there.
“Sis…”
Looking at Mr. Mikimoto, I saw him gazing at the same spot as me, tears streaming down his face.
“…Is she
gone now?”
When I asked, he nodded firmly.
“She's gone.
I can tell.{r}{p}…She won't come back.”
Everything was quiet, as if it had all been an illusion.
Even outside the window it was so still you could almost hear the snow piling up.
Mr. Mikimoto lifted {n2}'s body, laid her on the sofa, and covered her with his jacket.
I stood up unsteadily and gazed at her face.
“How did this happen?{r}{p}Why did you, in the first place…?”

“I'd been searching for evidence that someone in the Kobayashi family was the culprit all along.{r}{p}One day I heard a rumor that a ghost appears at this inn in winter.{r}{p}I was half skeptical, but even if it was only a rumor,
I thought that if I poked at it right, I might be able to draw out a confession from fear and guilt.”
“But talking about that in front of {n2} was a mistake after all.{r}{p}Most likely, the shocked {n2} and the lingering thoughts of my sister synchronized.
Perhaps {n2} herself came to hate her uncle and grandfather fiercely too.”
“In any case, what had been nothing more than a nuisance of a ghost turned into a terrifying demon.”
“Does {n2}…
remember?
What happened just now?”
If so, it's unbearable.
She had killed two people and nearly killed her own uncle.
If she had watched all of it from inside a body taken over by her mother…
Mr. Mikimoto shook his head.
“I don't know.{r}{p}If she did see it, she must be suffering an unimaginable shock.{r}{p}It might be impossible for her to recover…
by herself.”
He turned to me.
“You're the only one who can help her.{r}{p}Take care of her.”
I nodded, but I had no confidence at all.
But…
looking down at {n2}, whose face had grown haggard in such a short time, I thought.
All I can do is what I can do.
I tried to take {n2}'s hand and realized I was still gripping that charm tightly.
I'd held it so hard that I had to pry my stiff fingers open.
I pressed the charm into her hand, wrapped both of mine around it, and closed my eyes.
